sections.h2: Ways to sell a Greensboro house
sections.html:
Three paths are open in Greensboro: put the house on the market through an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept money from an investor who wants the property in whatever shape it is in. Repairs, calendar pressure and title questions decide which one wins.

Marketing through an agent fits a tidy home and an owner with patience for inspections and lender approvals. Going solo spares the agent commission, yet every contract form and pricing call lands on you. A direct cash deal shortens the calendar and ends the open houses, and the number offered reflects the renovation bill the buyer expects.

  • Pull the city's code compliance record for the address before you pick a route.
  • Ask Guilford County for the current tax balance on the parcel.
  • Collect any permits for additions, decks or finished basements.

Greensboro is a big city with its own planning, permit and housing departments. The city publishes council district lookups, which tell you which representative covers your street, and a rezoning notice for downtown owners. Owners close to the center should read the central business rezoning material before setting an asking figure, because a change in zoning can alter what gets built next door.

sections.h2: Code compliance problems and your sale
sections.html:
They can slow a closing. The city's Office of Code Compliance decides whether reported conditions violate the Code of Ordinances, and that code includes the Minimum Housing Code, the Land Development Ordinance and the Good Repair Ordinance.

Other rules in the same code cover nuisances, junked or abandoned vehicles and front yard parking. Open cases tend to surface during a buyer's due diligence. The city website has a case lookup, so type in your own address and resolve whatever shows, whether that is a neglected yard or a vehicle left to sit.

Anything built that required a permit should have one. Missing paperwork for an addition tends to stall closings, so assemble it early or tell the buyer exactly which pieces are absent.

A buyer who wants to run a rental needs a zoning permit before renting any dwelling for 30 days or less, and the city caps how many units a building may devote to that use.

  • Only residential dwelling units qualify, and the permit has to be posted inside the unit and in each listing.
  • One dwelling unit, or 25 percent of units in a multifamily building, is the ceiling.
  • Two adults per rented bedroom and one parked car per rented bedroom are the limits printed by the city.
  • A whole house host has to live in Guilford County or a neighboring county.

Council dropped the 750 foot spacing rule between rentals in 2025, and that was the only change. Applicants use the online portal or visit the Planner of the Day at the Melvin Municipal Office Building. If your house already holds a permit, ask the planning office whether it can pass to a buyer.

Guilford County put new real property values on the books as of January 1, 2026. The county did the work with its own appraisers after the state revenue department ordered a 2026 reappraisal in April 2023, citing homes selling above their assessed values. Rates are decided by elected officials in a separate step, set in June for the county's fiscal year.

For a seller, the new number is public. Anyone considering your house can see it, and a sharp jump from the 2022 figure may shape the negotiation. The county provides a sales comparison tool, a percentage change calculator and an online appeals platform. Questions can go to taxappraisal@guilfordcountync.gov or 336-641-4814.

Guilford County lists the kinds of documents it expects with a residential value dispute. They also double as a pre-listing checklist, because they show what a skeptical buyer would examine.

  • Sales of nearby comparable homes.
  • Photographs or reports of structural or system problems.
  • A recent professional appraisal.
  • Errors in square footage or other data on the property card.
  • Outside factors, with flood zone named as an example.

The county also offers a comparison tool called Comper Citizen, which shows an assessed value, the sales used to compare it and local trends. Open it and read your property card line by line. A wrong bedroom count or a missing garage affects both the tax bill and the buyer's view of the house.

Future challenges start with the county's review board and can continue to the state Property Tax Commission.

The statutory items are modest in number: a deed excise tax paid by the seller, recording fees collected by the register of deeds, and the annual property tax cycle.

Under G.S. 105-355 a parcel's unpaid levy attaches as a lien as of the listing date, which is why the title company asks for a payoff number. Ask the Guilford County tax office for it.

sections.h2: Tenants, a missed mortgage or an inherited title
sections.html:
Each of those situations runs on its own statutory clock, so identify yours early.

  • Notice to quit is seven days for monthly tenants and two days for weekly tenants.
  • The lender's foreclosure hearing notice has to reach the owner a minimum of 10 days beforehand.
  • Heirs of a modest estate (personal property net of liens under $20,000) may use a sworn affidavit, filed no sooner than 30 days after the death.
  • Seller financed contracts for homes of up to four units need recording, or a filed memorandum, in five business days.

Call your loan servicer first if payments are behind, then speak with a North Carolina attorney about the exact notice you hold. Bring the notice itself to that meeting, since the dates printed on it control the options that remain.

sections.h2: What to expect from a Greensboro closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, your attorney orders the title search, requests payoff letters and prepares the settlement statement. Ask to see it a day ahead and check the seller lines: excise tax, recording, the property tax split and any lien the search found.

Cash offers shorten this path because no lender is waiting on an appraisal. Listings add the buyer's loan and inspection, and a repair request can reopen price talks. Whichever route you choose, settle move-out timing and who keeps the appliances in writing before you sign.

faqs.q: Which office values my Greensboro house for tax?
faqs.a: Guilford County does, and its appraisal staff takes calls at 336-641-4814. Rates come afterward, set in budget decisions that the county describes as happening in June.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Guilford County value?
faqs.a: Gather comparable sales, photos of problems or an appraisal, and file with the county's review board during its appeal window. A further appeal can go to the state Property Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Can a buyer legally run a short term rental at a Greensboro house?
faqs.a: A city zoning permit is required, and only residential dwelling units qualify. Stays of 30 days or less count as short term rentals.

faqs.q: Which party pays transfer tax on a Greensboro deed?
faqs.a: The seller pays it at the register of deeds' office ahead of recording. The formula is a dollar for every $500 of value, with partial amounts rounded up.

faqs.q: How do I check a Greensboro address for open code violations?
faqs.a: Use the code compliance case lookup on the city website. It lists cases tied to an address, and the Office of Code Compliance can explain any entry.
